pages.text: "Why won't this rope come loose?" Rudi the hungry squirrel pulled the sled rope. It wound around their big tail, with a tight knot. "I want just one more ride before the dinner bell!"
Rudi bit the rope and yanked. The knot grew tighter. Their cheeks reddened, and their feet stamped. "Ugh! I hate it!"
Rudi kicked the sled hard. It slid downhill alone and crashed into a snow pile below. "Oh? My sled..." Rudi's voice stopped.

Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, ran over. "Rudi, it went all the way down!" Rudi sat in the snow and wrapped their tail around their body. "Now I can't have even one ride..." Their eyes were bright red.

Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, came downhill and sat warmly beside Rudi. "You felt hot inside, didn't you? Let the heat out. Angry? Breathe out—whoo!" She held a hand before her mouth and blew a white cloud of breath.
"Three times, like this. Whoo, whoo, whoo." Rudi held a hand before their mouth and blew too. Three white clouds rose and vanished. "Angry? Breathe out—whoo!"
Heat eased from Rudi's red cheeks. Their feet stopped stamping. Rudi looked at the knot again. Gently drawing the tail out made the rope slip loose. "Huh? It wouldn't come loose before!"
Rudi and Ppino went down to the snow pile and dug out the sled. "Sorry I shouted earlier." Rudi handed Ppino the rope. Ppino grinned and took it.
The sun rested on the peak. Time for just one ride remained. "One, when I'm angry, stop my hands first! Two, breathe out three times!" Rudi climbed onto the sled and zoomed downhill.
The dinner bell rang. Grandma lifted Rudi into a warm hug. Even in anger, three breaths out make hands gentle again. "Tomorrow I won't kick it. Angry? Breathe out—whoo!" Rudi said.
